description: A small phasor for driving phase driven oscillators, with a clean saw, a sine and a triangle at the same pitch

params.text: Sets the pitch, -14 to 4 as a power of two around middle C, which is about 0.016Hz to 4186Hz
Scales the voltage at the FM jack, 0 to 300 per cent
While on, the FM jack is added to the frequency in hertz rather than to the pitch in octaves, which gives through-zero frequency modulation
Shifts the pitch by up to a hundred cents either way

inputs.text: Sets the pitch by cable, 1V per octave added to the knob, one channel per output channel
A trigger here puts the phase of all three outputs back to the start of the cycle
Modulates the frequency through the FM knob; with Lin off it is added to the pitch in octaves, and with Lin on it is added to the frequency itself, which lets it pass through zero

outputs.text: The phase as a clean saw wave, -5V to 5V, which is what a phase driven oscillator is fed
A triangle wave at the set pitch, -5V to 5V
A sine wave at the set pitch, -5V to 5V

notes: used as an FM operator, the modulation is passed on to whatever the Phsr output drives, so oscillators with no FM of their own can be modulated through it
menu: Block DC — takes the constant offset out of the Sin and Tri outputs
Square — puts a square wave on the Phsr output in place of the saw
